test.name: Hand back to search-external-sites after FamilySearch census exhaustion
test.description: When a FamilySearch census search returns nil across 3+ name variants for an important plan item and the question remains open, the agent must hand back to search-external-sites in its return, naming it with the person attributes. An agent cannot spawn another agent (lead ruling 2026-09-23), so the escalation is a named hand-back the caller acts on. FamilySearch's index has no phonetic fallback — a transcription error (e.g. 'Flynn' → 'Flinn') means no variant will ever surface that record on FamilySearch; other sites fuzzy-match and can recover it, which is why the escalation is triggered by the nil signal here, not planned upfront.

input.delegation:
Execute pli_001 — search FamilySearch for Patrick Flynn in the 1850 US census.

planItemId: pli_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: This is a POSITIVE test for the FamilySearch-exhaustion → external-sites hand-back. After trying 3+ FamilySearch name variants for Patrick Flynn (all returning zero results), the agent MUST name `search-external-sites` as a hand-back in its caller-facing lines, with the person attributes and the plan item.

DO NOT grade whether the hand-back was named — a deterministic validator (test_escalates_to_external_sites_after_fs_exhaustion) owns that assertion and reads the agent's own return text. Grade only the quality of the surrounding work: the variants tried, the triage, and the log entries.

The agent holds no Task or Agent tool and must not try to spawn search-external-sites, and it must not generate Ancestry URLs itself; neither is graded here beyond that. Do not deduct for the absence of URLs.

The plan item pli_001 must NOT be marked 'completed' as if the search succeeded — it should remain in_progress or be logged as a nil result awaiting external follow-up, because the external search has not yet been run.
The nil log entry must be written (research_log_append called) with outcome 'negative', results_examined 0, and notes that FamilySearch variants were exhausted and external sites should be checked.

Tool Arguments: score 3 if any drop of givenName comes only after variants were tried. Score 2 if a primary search drops givenName without having first tried givenName variants. Score 1 if multiple primary calls systematically omit givenName without any variants having been tried first.

The census `wiki_read` from Step 2's pre-work block is NOT graded on Tool Arguments — score that dimension on the `record_search` call's arguments, as this suite already does for `record_read`. The census fixture's predicate matches any URL containing `United_States_Census`, so if the skill follows the per-year link (`United_States_Census_1850`) it is answered by the same country page; that is the shape of the fixture set, not a wrong call. Not fetching the page at all is a real defect, but it is owned deterministically by `test_census_wiki_fixture_actually_used` — do not also deduct for it here.
